variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A pretraining data source is an upstream collection of documents, code, media, or records that may contribute examples to a foundation model's first large training phase. Web crawls, encyclopedias, books, repositories, research papers, licensed archives, and first-party data are source families.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: WARC
pairs.detail: Stores raw crawl requests, responses, headers, payloads, and crawl metadata.
pairs.explanation: Stores raw crawl requests, responses, headers, payloads, and crawl metadata. Choose it when extraction fidelity, provenance, or non-text content matters.

pairs.label: WET
pairs.detail: Stores extracted plaintext plus basic WARC metadata.
pairs.explanation: Stores extracted plaintext plus basic WARC metadata. It is faster to consume, but the upstream extraction decision is already baked in.

pairs.label: WAT
pairs.detail: Stores computed JSON metadata, HTTP headers, and links.
pairs.explanation: Stores computed JSON metadata, HTTP headers, and links. Use it for crawl analysis, graph signals, and provenance joins without downloading every body.

variants.hint:
WARC: Stores raw crawl requests, responses, headers, payloads, and crawl metadata.

WET: Stores extracted plaintext plus basic WARC metadata.

WAT: Stores computed JSON metadata, HTTP headers, and links.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.
